title: The Gamma-Factorial Bridge: Γ(n+1) = n! Transfers All Stirling Facts
content: The entire proof architecture rests on gamma_eq_factorial (line 60): Real.Gamma (↑n + 1) = ↑(n.factorial) for all n : ℕ. This is a thin wrapper over Mathlib's Real.Gamma_nat_eq_factorial and is not a deep result, but it is the key lemma enabling every subsequent theorem. By rewriting with this equality, any proven fact about n! immediately yields the corresponding fact about Γ(n+1). The proof then never directly manipulates the Gamma integral: every theorem about Gamma at integer points reduces to a theorem about factorials, which can use the Stirling library directly.
mathContext: \Gamma(n+1) = n! \quad (n \in \mathbb{N})\\ \text{Bridge: rw [gamma\_eq\_factorial] converts } \Gamma \text{ goals to factorial goals}\\ \Gamma(1)=1,\; \Gamma(2)=1,\; \Gamma(n+1)=n\cdot\Gamma(n)

title: Gamma Stirling Equivalence: Transfer via Commutativity of Multiplication
content: gamma_isEquivalent_stirling (line 105) proves Γ(n+1) ~ √(2πn)·(n/e)^n. The proof: (1) rewrite the Gamma sequence as the factorial sequence (heq via gamma_eq_factorial); (2) note Mathlib's Stirling.factorial_isEquivalent_stirling uses √(2·n·π) while we use √(2·π·n); (3) prove hmul_comm by ring_nf (multiplication commutes); (4) rw [hmul_comm] and exact h. The ratio gamma_div_stirling_tendsto_one (Γ(n+1)/approx → 1) follows from isEquivalent_iff_tendsto_one, which requires the denominator to be eventually nonzero (gammaStirlingApprox_pos for n ≥ 1).
mathContext: \Gamma(n+1) \sim \sqrt{2\pi n}\cdot(n/e)^n\\ \frac{\Gamma(n+1)}{\sqrt{2\pi n}(n/e)^n} \to 1\\ \text{Note: Mathlib uses } \sqrt{2n\pi}, \text{ we use } \sqrt{2\pi n} \text{ (equal by commutativity)}

title: Gamma Lower Bound via stirlingSeq Antitonicity and ciInf
content: gamma_lower_bound (line 164) proves √(2πn)·(n/e)^n ≤ Γ(n+1) for n ≥ 1. The proof strategy: stirlingSeq n = n!/[√(2n)·(n/e)^n] is antitone (Stirling.stirlingSeq'_antitone) and tends to √π. By tendsto_atTop_ciInf, the infimum of the tail sequence equals the limit √π. Then ciInf_le gives stirlingSeq n ≥ √π at each n. Rearranging: n! ≥ √π·√(2n)·(n/e)^n = √(2πn)·(n/e)^n via the identity √π·√(2n) = √(2πn). The key step le_div_iff₀ converts the ratio inequality to a product inequality.

title: Γ(1/2) = √π from the Reflection Formula via Beta Function
content: gamma_one_half (line 331) proves Real.Gamma (1/2) = Real.sqrt π. The proof uses the reflection formula Γ(s)Γ(1-s) = π/sin(πs) at s=1/2: sin(π/2)=1 gives Γ(1/2)² = π. Since Γ(1/2) > 0 (Gamma positive on positives), Γ(1/2) = √π. The mathematical content: Γ(1/2) = ∫₀^∞ t^{-1/2}e^{-t}dt; substituting t=u² gives 2∫₀^∞ e^{-u²}du = √π (the Gaussian integral). Lean uses Mathlib's Real.Gamma_mul_Gamma_one_sub which encodes the reflection formula, combined with Real.sin_pi_div_two = 1 and a positivity argument to extract the square root.

title: Legendre Duplication Formula at Integer Points
content: duplication_at_nat (line 359) proves Γ(n)·Γ(n+1/2) = √π·Γ(2n)/4^{n-1} for n ≥ 1, a special case of the Legendre duplication formula Γ(x)Γ(x+1/2) = √π·2^{1-2x}·Γ(2x). At integers: Γ(n) = (n-1)!, Γ(2n) = (2n-1)!, and Γ(n+1/2) = (2n-1)!!·√π/2^n (from gamma_half_int_formula). The identity 4^{n-1} = 2^{2n-2} arises from 2^{1-2n} = 2/4^n. The proof uses Real.Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_one from Mathlib (encoding B(x,x+1/2)) and simplifies via the integer Gamma values. The duplication formula generalizes Γ(2n) = 2^{2n-1}/√π · Γ(n)·Γ(n+1/2).

title: Γ(n+1/2) = (2n-1)!! · √π / 2^n by Induction on Double Factorial
content: gamma_half_int_formula (line 457) proves by induction on n. Base n=0: Γ(1/2) = 1·√π/1 (gamma_one_half). Inductive step: Γ((k+1)+1/2) = Γ((k+1/2)+1) = (k+1/2)·Γ(k+1/2) by Real.Gamma_add_one. Substituting IH: (k+1/2)·(df(k)·√π/2^k) = (2k+1)/2·df(k)·√π/2^k = (2k+1)·df(k)·√π/2^{k+1} = df(k+1)·√π/2^{k+1}. The Lean proof uses push_cast to lift ℕ-arithmetic to ℝ, then field_simp + ring. doubleFactorial (line 449) is defined inductively: df(0)=1, df(k+1)=(2k+1)·df(k), so df(n) = 1·3·5···(2n-1).

title: Central Binomial C(2n,n) = 4^nΓ(n+1/2) / (√πΓ(n+1)): Two Representations
content: centralBinom_via_gamma (line 488) proves C(2n,n) = Γ(2n+1)/Γ(n+1)² by rewriting Gammas as factorials and using Nat.choose_mul_factorial_mul_factorial. centralBinom_gamma_half_int (line 532) gives the half-integer representation: C(2n,n) = 4^nΓ(n+1/2)/(√πΓ(n+1)), connecting central binomials to the Gamma function at non-integer points. The key lemma factorial_double_mul (line 514) proves (2n)! = 2^n·(2n-1)!!·n! by induction. This identity, combined with Γ(n+1/2) = (2n-1)!!·√π/2^n, gives C(2n,n) = 4^n/(√π·√ n) asymptotically via Stirling.
